result.reply:
Two separate things here, and I want to be careful not to conflate them.

First: has anyone actually shown me the diff? What I've got is a description — "loads everything into memory instead of streaming." That's enough for me to reason about the situation, but if this is heading toward an actual approve/request-changes, I need the real diff, not the summary. Riley might be doing something in between (e.g., chunked reads that still land in one list) that reads differently than "loads everything" makes it sound.

On the substance, assuming the description holds: this isn't a detail-level deviation, it's a core-approach one. Streaming in batches wasn't an implementation nicety Marcus picked arbitrarily — the plan's stated reason was to keep memory bounded. Loading everything into memory doesn't get to the same place by a different route; it drops the actual guarantee. Passing the ticket's acceptance criteria doesn't cover that, because the criteria describe output correctness, not memory behavior under a large export — that's exactly the "satisfies the letter while missing the point" case.

And nobody flagged it. If Riley had said "went with in-memory, dataset sizes don't justify streaming complexity yet" — that's a build-time call I'd weigh on its merits, could well be fine. But silence plus a plan that explicitly called out the constraint means the gap itself is the finding, before I even get to whether in-memory is acceptable.

So: blocking, not a nit. Needs either the batching implemented per plan, or an explicit conversation with Marcus about why the constraint doesn't apply here (data volume is small, there's a size cap elsewhere, whatever) — not merged silently either way. Get me the actual diff and I'll look at what's really there before this goes back to Riley.
